strengths: The problem has an identifiable audience in representation learning, program analysis, and reverse engineering. Transferring information from source code and comments into an encoder used without those modalities downstream is a useful research direction.

The architecture diagrams communicate the main design clearly: a frozen semantic encoder, a trainable binary representation encoder, and scalar or featurewise interpolation followed by contrastive learning.

The evaluation covers four complementary tasks, component ablations, and a CodeT5 extension. Reported improvements are encouraging, including function-name accuracy of 33.41% versus RoBERTa’s 29.41%, and summarization BLEU-4 of 34.36 versus GraphCodeBERT’s 32.43.
weaknesses: Necessary—resolve the POJ-104 task contradiction. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify non-overlapping training, development, and test labels, with 64/16/24 problems, but Section 4.2 describes supervised classification into 104 classes. No mechanism for predicting unseen classes is provided. If the experiment is actually retrieval, specify the query and candidate sets, relevance criterion, and metric computation; otherwise provide a valid classification protocol. This ambiguity undermines Tables 3, 7, and 8, including the principal ablation evidence.

Necessary—align the application claims with the evaluated inputs. The experiments use compiler-generated LLVM IR, rather than representations recovered from stripped native executables. Figures 6–8 retain informative function and type names, and function-name stripping is described only for the name-recovery experiment. These representations are not trivially interchangeable, as the introductory footnote asserts. Evaluate the claimed stripped-binary setting or consistently narrow the conclusions to the documented LLVM setting. Function-name recovery should also be qualified as classification among 91 frequent names.

Necessary—make the objective and implementation reproducible. Equation (4) omits the softmax stated in the prose, leaving raw similarities that need not constitute probability targets for Equation (5). Specify the actual objective, normalization, gradient flow through the targets, and modality sampling. The encoder checkpoints, interpolation-network dimensions, downstream generation decoder, and compilation settings also need concrete descriptions; the current conceptual account does not determine the implemented system.

Necessary—separate interpolation benefits from additional training. The no-interpolation/PCL model receives 10 epochs, whereas the full model receives 30 or 70. The assertion that PCL converged does not establish a controlled comparison. Comparable training budgets and separate interpolation-stage controls are needed to substantiate the component claims. Section 5.3’s reported greater-than-97% deterioration under joint objectives also lacks sufficient objective definitions and diagnostics. Single-seed results provide little support for robustness claims, particularly for small differences such as 25.16% versus 24.73% reconstruction exact match.

Necessary—clarify evaluation construction and reference provenance. Section 3.2 says generation is evaluated on validation data, while Section 4.3 describes test-set evaluation. Specify pretraining, downstream training, model-selection, and evaluation partitions, together with overlap checks across the GitHub-derived corpora. Clarify whether summarization references are CodeT5-generated and document their construction. The manuscript does not establish leakage, but its reporting is insufficient to assess independence and what agreement with the reference summaries measures.

Necessary—support or narrow claims of semantic correctness and human comprehension. BLEU, GLEU, ROUGE, and exact match primarily measure agreement with reference text; no systematic functional validation or human evaluation supports the stronger conclusions. The qualitative examples are insufficient: Figure 7’s summary of pyb_main omits its configuration update, and Figure 8 displays a shift expression without an operand. These examples require correction and verification. Semantic validation is needed for functional claims; otherwise the findings should be limited to the reported text metrics.

Necessary—correct the embedding interpretation. Section 4.1 argues that unique programs should not cluster and that the t-SNE visualization proves improved embedding quality. Unique programs can share semantics, and distances across independently produced t-SNE plots do not establish improved semantic geometry. Remove these deductions or replace them with quantitative evidence. The human gradual-learning analogy should likewise be presented as motivation. Together with the protocol and scope problems above, these issues constitute a substantive failure of the evidential acceptance criterion.

Optional improvements: streamline repetitive motivational prose, repair dangling citations and inconsistent dataset/metric names, and provide preprocessing code and trained checkpoints to make the work easier to build on.
